subject: Deployment mode & cost follow-up — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@finedge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode & cost follow-up — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Samir —

Great to chat earlier today. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned on the deployment-mode qualification and the cost ask you mentioned: 

Recap from call:
- Primary goal: embed FinEdge customer support assistant into your claims flow. Must support low latency (95th < 250ms) and PHI-safe storage for a subset of transcripts.
- Traffic signal: peak spikes around business hours; you mentioned up to ~50 RPS peak, but average QPS likely much lower.
- Security & compliance: SOC 2 + KMS integration required; potential on-prem requirement for PHI handling depending on compliance lawyer review.
- Timeline: pilot in Q4, production in early Q1.

Specific asks I took away:
1) High-level cost comparison for Hosted API (per-token) vs Dedicated (reserved capacity / monthly commit) vs Private (VPC / on-prem) — include example numbers and break-even points.
2) SLA and security doc we can share with legal.
3) A short MUTUAL ACTION PLAN and a time to review the numbers with your infra team.

I've attached a starter cost model (redwood_cost_modeling_v2.xlsx) with assumptions you can tweak, and a short SLA/security summary. Below is a quick baseline I can iterate on — if you can confirm average tokens per request and rough monthly request volume I'll tighten estimates.

Baseline assumptions (please confirm):
- Avg tokens per request: 450
- Estimated monthly requests: 3,000,000 (update from your infra team if different)
- Peak concurrency: 50 RPS

Initial high-level comparison (ballpark):
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): per-1k-token rate, example $0.020 / 1k tokens -> ~ $27k/month under above assumptions. No infra commitment, fastest to prod.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): baseline reserved instance + lower marginal cost. Example: reserved pool ~$45k–$65k/month for baseline capacity to meet latency/SLOs + $0.010 / 1k tokens for overage -> total depends on commit level. Better if sustained, predictable throughput.
- Private / On-prem: higher fixed setup and infra ops; example TCO varies, initial ramp often >$150k+ one-time + ongoing infra costs. Best when PHI cannot leave customer-controlled network.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm tokens/request and estimated monthly request volume?
- If you're OK, I'll put together 2 pricing scenarios: (A) Pilot (hosted + limited reserved buffer) and (B) Production (dedicated reserved commit) with explicit numbers and break-even analysis.

Thanks — will sync with Marissa and Neha on the model and loop back tomorrow with more detail.

—
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Aditya —

Quick answers:
- Avg tokens/request: 420–480 (let's use 450 as a midpoint).
- Monthly requests: rough estimate 2.5M–4M (we currently see ~3M active requests in pre-prod; could be higher in prod).
- PHI handling: legal says any PHI must be kept in customer-controlled environment. That suggests we need either Private VPC with customer KMS or a Hybrid approach where PHI flows are routed to Private/Dedicated and non-PHI traffic can be hosted.
- Latency target: 95th < 250ms.

Can you model a hybrid recommendation: Dedicated pool for low-latency user-facing traffic + Private for PHI subset? Also need an example of reserved commit tiers and the guaranteed SLOs attached.

Let's sync live next week with infra — can you propose two times? Tue or Wed morning PST works for us.

Samir
Head of Product
FinEdge Inc.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & cost follow-up — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Samir — thanks for the quick clarifications, that helps a lot. Attached is an updated sheet (redwood_cost_modeling_v2.xlsx) — I've included a hybrid scenario as requested. Summary below with the numbers filled in using your midpoint assumptions (450 tokens/request, 3.2M requests/month):

Assumptions used:
- Avg tokens/request: 450
- Monthly requests: 3,200,000
- Monthly tokens = 3.2M * 450 = 1.44 billion tokens/month

Scenario A — Hosted (pay-as-you-go)
- Price used for example: $0.020 / 1k tokens
- Cost = (1,440,000,000 / 1,000) * $0.020 = $28,800/month
- Pros: No infra commitments, fastest setup; cons: higher per-unit cost at scale and no isolation for PHI.

Scenario B — Dedicated reserved commit (production)
- Example reserved pool: $55,000/month baseline to meet your latency SLO at 50 RPS peak (includes GPU infra, ops, basic SLA)
- Marginal overage: $0.010 / 1k tokens
- For 1.44B tokens: overage cost = (1,440,000 * $0.010) = $14,400 -> Total = $69,400/month
- Pros: Predictable performance and improved unit economics as commit increases; cons: higher fixed cost.

Scenario C — Hybrid (Dedicated + Private for PHI)
- Assume 10% of traffic touches PHI (you confirm).
- Private VPC for PHI: set-up & managed private deployment (customer KMS): indicative incremental cost: one-time onboarding ~ $120k + ongoing infra ops ~ $12k/month (varies by region).
- Hybrid monthly run-rate (assuming 10% PHI routed to Private, 90% to Dedicated):
  - Dedicated portion (90% tokens): 1.296B tokens -> treated under Dedicated reserved pool above (no change to baseline reserved sizing in many cases)
  - Private portion (10% tokens): additional infra ops ~$12k/month + reserved minimal compute for PHI bursts.
- Net example first-month total (including one-time onboarding): ~ $200k (onboarding) + $69k/month baseline + $12k/month private ops = ~$281k in month 1, then ~ $81k/month ongoing (approx).

Break-even guidance:
- If monthly tokens exceed ~3.5B tokens, Dedicated reserved pricing generally becomes more attractive vs Hosted at the example rates above. Exact threshold depends on reserved pool price and utilization.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I'll update the spreadsheet with a sensitivity table (vary tokens/request, % PHI, reserved commit tiers) so your infra/legal can tweak assumptions.
2) Schedule 30m with infra next Tue (7/21) or Wed (7/22) morning PST — propose Tue 9:30am PST.
3) If you want, I can follow-up with a short commercial term sheet (quote) for a 6-month pilot (small reserved buffer + hosted fallback) vs a 12-month committed production quote.

Links & attachments: cost model in Drive, and the SLA/security PDF included for legal.

—
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_cost_modeling_v2.xlsx; SLA_and_Security_Summary.pdf
